title: The modern church, looking back
hook: Tubman, Bonhoeffer, Romero, Tutu, and a global church
tomorrow: Christmas, or every Sunday: which one is the real feast?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the reformations: a plowboy promise, a line from Romans, a sword refused, and wounds still healing. Reformed and reforming. Now, a crowd in the stands.
screen: `REFORMED AND REFORMING.` → `A CROWD IN THE STANDS.`

segments.voice: From the track, the people in the stands are a blur of color. The letter to the Hebrews runs through a long list of the faithful, Abraham, Moses, Rahab and more, and then reaches for an odd word: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.” Then it tells the reader to lay aside every weight and run. A cloud? Why call a crowd of people who have already died a cloud?
screen: `A BLUR IN THE STANDS.` → `SO GREAT A CLOUD.` → `WHY A CLOUD?`

segments.voice: Hebrews doesn't explain the word, so readers offer answers. One: a cloud surrounds you. You don't watch it from a distance; you're inside it. Two: a cloud is many drops that read as one, and the witnesses are many lives that read as one story. Either way, notice what they're for. They aren't judges waiting for someone to trip. They ran first, and because they're there, the runner can lay aside the weight. And the cloud kept growing. Harriet Tubman escaped slavery, then went back to lead others out, and spoke of praying as she went. Dietrich Bonhoeffer, a German Lutheran pastor, spoke against the Nazi regime and was executed by it. Óscar Romero, archbishop of San Salvador, spoke up for the poor and was shot while celebrating Mass. Desmond Tutu, an Anglican archbishop, worked against apartheid in South Africa, and spoke of ubuntu, a word from southern Africa he explained roughly as: a person is a person through other people. Different churches, countries, dangers. Behind them, a church praying in Lagos and Seoul, São Paulo and Manila. Some churches formally name saints; others remember their people in prayer and song. Both keep the cloud in view.
screen: `A CLOUD SURROUNDS YOU.` · `MANY DROPS, ONE STORY.` · `THEY RAN FIRST.` · `TUBMAN, BONHOEFFER, ROMERO, TUTU.` · then, large: `THE CLOUD OF WITNESSES.`

segments.voice: Write one name by hand: a modern witness from today, or someone from your own life whose faith or courage ran ahead of you, a grandparent, a teacher, a neighbor. Under it, write the one weight they helped you lay down. If you pray, give thanks for them through the sit.
The modern church. Tubman, Bonhoeffer, Romero, Tutu, and a church praying in many languages: the cloud, still growing.
Hold onto this: the cloud of witnesses, who ran first so others could keep running. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1773 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 22 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: CHRISTMAS, OR EVERY SUNDAY? WHICH IS THE FEAST?`

original.note: Greek: a cloud, a great mass. Hebrews 12:1 uses it for the crowd of witnesses.

trapdoor: what you thought: a cloud of witnesses means spectators watching you.
what it means: those who ran first surround the runner, so the weight can be laid aside.
what a scholar hears: Hebrews 12:1 follows the list of the faithful in chapter 11; the Greek nephos is a cloud, and the text never says why it chose that word.
guess: the church of recent centuries and its witnesses
the first churches founded by the apostles
a council that wrote the creeds

chat.says: concert's in 2 days. pop will be in surgery, dad's on shift. who'll even be in the seats?
options: More than it looks: a cloud of witnesses, plus Nia. Pop and Dad ran ahead for you.
Nobody who counts. If family can't come, the seats are basically empty.
Don't think about the seats at all; sing to an empty room in your head.
chat.meaning: Hebrews pictures those who ran first surrounding the runner like a cloud, so the weight can be laid aside. The seats are fuller than they look.
